assets.title: How to test your MarketingOS account
assets.content:
Subject: How to test your MarketingOS account
Preview text: Start with one real offer and one email; the result is evidence for or against a complete sequence.

Hi there,

MarketingOS turns source material from a SaaS offer into a launch or onboarding email you can inspect before deciding whether to test a complete sequence.

Someone unfamiliar with the product reads the draft before you receive it, and passages that did not land are rewritten. You still check the facts, links and brand voice before using the copy.

In your existing account, paste website text or add a PDF or screenshot, then ask for the email in your own words. A generation can take several minutes.

One email will not validate a complete campaign. It will show whether the draft—and the editing it still needs—make a full launch or onboarding sequence worth testing.

Open your MarketingOS account → https://app.orqagent.com/login/

- the MarketingOS founder

report.request: Write exactly two English emails introducing MarketingOS to invited early-access testers who already have a test account. They run a small SaaS business and need to write a launch or onboarding email campaign. Explain one concrete supported reason to try the product, then invite them to test one real offer and review the output. brief.interpretation: This is a two-email onboarding sequence for invited early-access testers who already have MarketingOS accounts, not a sales or public-signup campaign. The selected readers operate small SaaS businesses and have a real launch or onboarding offer they can use for a bounded product test.
brief.reader:
Selected audience (user-stated constraints): Invited early-access testers with an existing account who operate a small SaaS business and need launch or onboarding email copy..
No further recipient situation is established. Compiled market context is research to check for applicability, not a replacement biography.
brief.reader_segment: an invited pilot user with one real offer to test and the founder waiting on her notes
brief.reader_profile_override: Invited early-access testers with an existing account who operate a small SaaS business and need launch or onboarding email copy.
brief.promise: A bounded test using one real SaaS offer lets an invited user judge MarketingOS from a grounded, reviewed draft and the work required to make it usable, without committing a full campaign to the test.
brief.orientation: MarketingOS is an email campaign drafting and market-research application that turns supplied offer material and a plain-language request into reviewed draft email copy for the account holder to check and transfer into their own sending tool.
brief.arc: Email one moves the reader from having an unused pilot account to requesting one narrowly scoped email from real offer material. Email two moves them from treating the returned copy as prose to like or dislike toward checking its factual grounding, cold-reader response and required edits.
brief.sequence_rationale: The sequence starts with the smallest useful action because these readers already have access and do not need a sales argument: one offer, its real material and one requested email. The second email explains how to evaluate the result rather than repeating the activation instructions, using source facts to check what the draft claims and reader feedback to find what was unclear to someone without product knowledge. Each email stands alone and sends the reader to the existing-account login. The campaign does not raise price, performance, testimonials or public availability because none is established, and it does not imply that MarketingOS sends the resulting campaign. The single thing that would most change this campaign is the confirmed subscription price and whether a free trial or free tier exists.

emails.job: Get the invited user to run a small first test: sign in, add material for one real SaaS offer, and request one launch or onboarding email.
emails.single_idea: Test MarketingOS on one real offer and one email before deciding whether to entrust it with a complete launch or onboarding sequence.
emails.felt_need: The reader needs launch or onboarding copy for a real SaaS offer and should be able to test the product without making the first run a full-campaign exercise.
emails.mechanism: The reader signs in to the existing account, supplies the offer's website material, pasted text, PDF or screenshot, and asks in plain English for one launch or onboarding email. MarketingOS can then generate a reviewed draft from that material.
emails.belief_shift: Before: trying MarketingOS means handing it an entire campaign brief. After: one real offer and one requested email are enough for a useful first check.
must_not_say: Do not call this a signup, free trial, purchase or public offer; the reader already has an invited account.
Do not mention a price, discount, subscription term or future commercial terms.
Do not promise better opens, clicks, conversions, revenue or less editing.
Do not assume the reader's present writing tools, sending platform, team, list, results or urgency.
Do not describe MarketingOS as an agent builder or mention Slack bots, integrations or credits.
Do not broaden the first action into competitor research, audience research, LinkedIn work or a complete campaign.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS account, add the real material for one offer, and request one launch or onboarding email at https://app.orqagent.com/login/.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the first draft is relevant enough to justify testing a complete launch or onboarding sequence.
emails.next_step_value: The existing account lets the reader supply real offer material, describe the requested email in their own words and generate a reviewed draft.
emails.next_step_limit: One requested email tests a narrow drafting task; it does not establish the quality or performance of a complete campaign.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the bounded action unmistakable—one real offer and one email—so the subject reads as an account activation prompt rather than a product launch or sales pitch.

emails.job: Get the invited user to review the generated email through two specific lenses—source accuracy and cold-reader comprehension—and record useful pilot feedback.
emails.single_idea: Inspecting the source facts and reader feedback separates two different questions: whether the draft says only what the offer supports, and whether someone unfamiliar with the product can follow it.
emails.felt_need: A draft can sound plausible while containing a factual error or losing a reader who does not already understand the product.
emails.mechanism: MarketingOS first compiles supplied material into facts it is allowed to claim, then has the draft read by someone without product knowledge and rewrites what did not land. The pilot user can review that grounding and feedback alongside the returned text, then note phrases to keep or rewrite, factual errors and time spent editing.
emails.belief_shift: Before: reviewing the output is mainly a judgment about whether the prose sounds good. After: it is a structured check of factual grounding, reader comprehension and the editing still required.
must_not_say: Do not claim that the fact set prevents every error or that cold-reader review guarantees clarity.
Do not imply that MarketingOS removes the user's responsibility to check facts, links or brand voice.
Do not imply that MarketingOS sends, publishes or installs the drafts in an email platform.
Do not promise that editing will be faster than writing from scratch.
Do not introduce prices, testimonials, performance claims or sector-wide quality claims.
Do not revisit the input instructions as the main argument; this email is about evaluating the output.
emails.objection: The reader still has to review every draft before using it.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS account and review the draft against its source facts and reader feedback at https://app.orqagent.com/login/.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide which parts of the draft are usable, what must be corrected or rewritten, and whether the result merits another run.
emails.next_step_value: The review gives the reader a concrete way to identify phrases worth keeping, factual errors, comprehension problems and the time required to edit the draft.
emails.next_step_limit: This inspection does not validate campaign performance or replace the user's final checks and transfer into their own sending tool.
emails.subject_strategy: Frame the open around how to judge the completed run—facts first, then what reached a reader—rather than asking generally for feedback.
must_not_reuse: Test MarketingOS on one real offer and one email before deciding whether to entrust it with a complete launch or onboarding sequence.

brief.voice_notes: Use precise, mechanism-first English with one developed idea per paragraph. Long explanatory sentences may use em dashes or colons, but pair them with short statements of scope and limits. Address the reader as an existing account holder. Avoid hype, superlatives, generic AI language and any vocabulary associated with the older orqAgent product.
